title: A Cipher for the Letter
premise: Mirabel Delacroix, the coroner of Bellhaven, has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, earning her a reputation as a woman who reads bodies like letters. When a missing person's diary arrives in her mail—continuing entries past the date its owner, postmaster Elias Wren, vanished—she discovers the diary names a witness everyone swears is dead: her own presumed-dead mother, whose death certificate Mirabel signed years ago. As the statute of limitations on the old crime ticks down, Mirabel and Elias, found alive but hiding, must untangle a conspiracy that reaches into the town's founding families. In the end, Mirabel exposes the killer at the courthouse steps, chooses love over the duty that once isolated her, and learns her mother faked her death to protect her—and is still alive.
about_author: Tamsin Thornbury spent a decade as a rural records clerk before turning to fiction, a job that taught her how much truth hides in filing cabinets. She writes mysteries from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where she keeps an annotated map of every fictional town she's invented.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Establishes Bellhaven, its graveyard, and Mirabel's habit of speaking to the dead by name as she closes her third 'accident' case. Emotional beat: competent loneliness; she knows every grave but no one truly knows her.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A package arrives containing Elias Wren's diary—with entries dated after his disappearance six months ago. The final entry names a witness: 'M.D., alive.' Emotional beat: dread mixed with electric purpose.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Weather
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. She reviews the three 'accidental' deaths and finds they share one thread: all were connected to the 1998 Harrow Mill fire. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the accidents were a pattern, and patterns have authors.

chapters.title: A Man Who Refused to Be Dead
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Revealed hiding in a lakeside cabin, Elias explains why he staged his vanishing: the diary's earlier entries made him a target. He mailed it to Mirabel because she signed his mother's death certificate—and he suspects she signs things too easily. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Strangers at a Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Mirabel confronts Elias; trust is negotiated over bad coffee. They agree to work together until the statute expires in five weeks. Emotional beat: wary alliance, first spark of something warmer.

chapters.title: The Founding Families' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Digging through county archives, they find Harrow Mill was torched for insurance by a consortium including the Ashcombe family—now Bellhaven's beloved first citizens. Emotional beat: the sick thrill of pulling a thread that unravels a whole town.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Sign
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The witness 'M.D.' is Marguerite Delacroix—Mirabel's mother, dead nineteen years by Mirabel's own certification. Flashbacks reveal Mirabel was handed the file and told not to look closely. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias's cabin is searched while they're away; a warning note quotes the diary verbatim. Someone inside law enforcement is feeding information to the Ashcombes. Emotional beat: paranoia; safety was always an illusion.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Cried Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Deputy Corliss Ashcombe offers Mirabel 'protection,' revealing he knows about the diary. Elias realizes Corliss is stalling them until the statute expires. Emotional beat: the enemy wears a friendly face.

chapters.title: Grave Visit
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At her mother's grave, Mirabel finds fresh flowers and soil disturbed—the casket holds sandbags. Her mother may be alive, and someone visits her plot. Emotional beat: grief overturned like the coffin itself.

chapters.title: Letters to a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Following the flower trail, they find a PO box rented under Marguerite's maiden name. Inside: unmailed letters addressed to Mirabel, each one apologizing. Emotional beat: tenderness and fury in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Third Death Was a Message
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Re-examining victim three, they realize he wasn't silenced—he was killed trying to deliver evidence to Marguerite. The evidence never arrived. Emotional beat: urgency; the clock is now four weeks.

chapters.title: Ashcombe Gala
chapters.summary: POV alternating. They infiltrate the Ashcombes' charity gala; Mirabel dances with patriarch Edmund Ashcombe, who quotes her mother's handwriting back to her—a threat wrapped in charm. Emotional beat: love against duty, as Elias watches and Mirabel plays a role she hates.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Their safehouse burns. Elias pulls Mirabel out, badly burning his hands saving the diary. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into devotion; neither can pretend this is just a case anymore.

chapters.title: Confession in a Storm Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Sheltering overnight, Elias confesses he knew Marguerite was alive—he was her courier and abandoned her when the danger grew. Mirabel must forgive him or lose him. Emotional beat: love tested against duty's oldest lie.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Using the letters' cipher—a code based on gravestone epitaphs—they trace Marguerite to a convent two counties over. Emotional beat: breathless hope; the impossible is a bus ride away.

chapters.title: Mother
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The reunion is not tender: Marguerite refuses to testify, believing the Ashcombes will kill Mirabel if she does. Mother and daughter fight with nineteen years of silence between them. Emotional beat: heartbreak; rescue doesn't equal reunion.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Three days left. Corliss arrests Elias on fabricated charges, and the diary is seized as evidence—by the people it condemns. Emotional beat: despair at its floor; every door locked at once.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Mirabel turns her unique weapon on the town: she exhumes the third victim publicly, forcing an inquest where she presents her full findings from the stand. Emotional beat: quiet ferocity; the coroner finally speaks for the dead out loud.

chapters.title: The Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Climax. Marguerite, moved by Mirabel's public stand, arrives to testify as the statute expires at noon. Corliss attempts to stop her; Edmund's confession is caught on the inquest recorder when he threatens them openly. Emotional beat: triumph snatched from the jaws of the deadline.

chapters.title: Reckoning Season
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Aftermath: arrests, resignations, the town reckoning with what it chose not to see. Corliss flips on his father. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; justice is anticlimactic and still worth it.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Letter
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Epilogue. Mirabel decodes her mother's final letter—it was never a cipher, just a mother afraid her plain words would be read. She chooses to stay in Bellhaven, with Elias, no longer alone among the graves. Emotional beat: belonging; found family, chosen love, identity reclaimed.
